t: This is St Olave's Court, a small alley in the City of London. It takes its name from Saint Olaf, also called Olaf II, who was King of Norway from 1015 to 1028. He died at the Battle of Stiklestad in 1030 and was canonized at Nidaros the following year. His remains were enshrined in Nidaros Cathedral. His sainthood encouraged the spread of Christianity among Scandinavia's Norsemen, and his name lives on here in a London alley.
